displayName: Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification

tests.name: Add command to .bash_profile
tests.description: Adds a command to the .bash_profile file of the current user

tests.name: Add command to .bashrc
tests.description: Adds a command to the .bashrc file of the current user

tests.name: Add command to .shrc
tests.description: Adds a command to the .shrc file of the current user

tests.name: Append to the system shell profile
tests.description: An adversary may wish to establish persistence by executing malicious commands from the systems /etc/profile every time "any" user logs in.

tests.name: Append commands user shell profile
tests.description: An adversary may wish to establish persistence by executing malicious commands from the users ~/.profile every time the "user" logs in.

tests.name: System shell profile scripts
tests.description: An adversary may wish to establish persistence by adding commands into any of the script files in the /etc/profile.d/ directory, which are executed every time "any" user logs in.

tests.name: Create/Append to .bash_logout
tests.description:
The Bash shell runs ~/.bash_logout "if it exists" to run commands on user logout. An adversary may create or append to a .bash_logout to clear history, start processes etc. Note the ~/.bash_logout is only run if you explicitly exit or log out of an "interactive login shell session" i.e. via the console, SSH, /bin/bash -l or su -l <username>. 

This test creates the art user, logs in, creates a .bash_logout which will echo some text into the art.txt file on logout and logs out and the /home/art/art.txt is created.
